title: Introduce soft-egress-sheath and backoff-watcher to reduce regional KV pressure
author: Riley Chen
description: Motivation: We observed recurring short-lived regional KV pressure during bursty tenant egress that caused elevated tail latencies and intermittent circuit flips. This hotpatch introduces a lightweight "soft egress sheath" that applies a conservative, latency-aware soft deny at the egress gate and a separate background "backoff-watcher" process which tracks KV pressure signals (drain latency, stall rate, KV refill lag) to progressively escalate or relax the sheath. Goals: reduce cascade circuit flips, preserve fast-path latency for healthy tenants, and provide clear telemetry for postmortem. What changed: 1) runtime/egress/sheath.go: new soft-eject policy (token-aware, per-tenant) and adaptive weighting logic. 2) runtime/egress/backoff_watcher.go: background worker that ingests KV pressure metrics and emits sheath control events via the existing routing-policy bus. 3) telemetry/metrics_registry.go: 4 new metrics (egress_sheath_level, egress_sheath_decisions, kv_pressure_score, backoff_watcher_health) and one new tag on existing latency histograms (egress_sheath=on/off). 4) sre/alerts/egress_sheath.rule: temporary Prometheus alerts for >90th pct sheath_level and watcher unhealthy. 5) docs/ops/egress_sheath.md: operator runbook and rollback steps. 6) tests/egress/sheath_test.go and integration/egress_workload_sim_test.go: unit and integration harnesses with mocked KV slowdowns. Compatibility: The sheath is a runtime policy with safe defaults (initially disabled) and can be toggled per-region via feature flag. The backoff-watcher uses only read-only telemetry and does not alter persisted state. Safety checklist: - [x] Opt-in feature flag gate in runtime config - [x] Unit tests for adaptive weighting and decision boundaries - [x] Integration tests with synthetic KV stalls - [x] SRE smoke runbook and temporary alerts - [x] Post-deploy validation queries included in release notes Testing & validation: Local unit tests run (go test ./runtime/egress -run TestSheath*), integration job executed in canary region against a KV harness with ramped delays, and synthetic load tests show 45-60% reduction in circuit flips in synthetic surge scenarios while tail latency for healthy tenants increased by <1ms. Rollout plan: Canary deploy to us-east-1 with feature flag on for 10% of regional routing for 2 hours, inspect metrics and alert thresholds, then 50% for 1 hour, then global rollout if stable. Rollback plan: flip feature flag off; backoff-watcher is designed to silently stop emitting control events. Related work: follows observations from ENG-2142; complements previously-merged egress tapering heuristics. Notes: This is intentionally conservative: sheath decisions are weighted by tenant SLA class and never preempt dedicated-capacity routes.

review_thread: Hannah Park (reviewer): Can we ensure sheath decisions never affect dedicated capacity routes? Author: Yes — decisions carry a "route_class" guard; added tests to validate. (resolved)

Miguel Alvarez (reviewer): Backoff-watcher seems to sample KV metrics every 5s — will that amplify telemetry load? Author: Sampling uses existing aggregated windows and applies local smoothing; added metrics to monitor watcher cost. (resolved)

release_notes: Hotfix: soft egress sheath + backoff watcher to reduce KV-pressure-induced circuit flips. Opt-in via feature flag. Adds telemetry and SRE alerts. See docs/ops/egress_sheath.md for rollout and rollback instructions.
notes_for_ops: Runbook: (1) Enable feature flag in region using console or CLI. (2) Monitor egress_sheath_level and kv_pressure_score; if watcher unhealthy, disable immediately. (3) To rollback, flip flag to false; watcher will drain. Temporary alerts are in sre/alerts/egress_sheath.rule. Follow staged canary rollout described in PR description.
testing: Unit: go test ./runtime/egress -run TestSheath* (local). Integration: integration/egress_workload_sim_test with KV delay profiles (CI harness). Canary: deploy to us-east-1 at 10% traffic, monitor for 2 hours; if healthy increase to 50% then global. Metrics to watch: egress_sheath_level, circuit_flips, kv_pressure_score, p99 latency per tenant class.
